holidays.name: National Toasted Marshmallow Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the gooey, golden-brown joy of marshmallows roasted over a fire, stovetop, or backyard fire pit. Perfect for s'mores, or for eating them straight off the stick with slightly singed fingers.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday popular with food-day calendars, timed to the end of summer camping season when campfire treats are at their peak.
holidays.funFact: Marshmallows were originally made from the sap of the marshmallow plant, a root used by ancient Egyptians as a sweet treat for the gods and royalty.

holidays.name: International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances
holidays.description: A serious United Nations observance that raises awareness of people who have been forcibly disappeared and supports their families in seeking truth and justice.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN General Assembly in 2010 and first observed in 2011, following decades of advocacy by families of the disappeared, particularly in Latin America.
holidays.funFact: The day is often marked with blue forget-me-not flowers, which symbolize remembrance.

holidays.name: Frankenstein Day
holidays.description: A spooky-yet-literary celebration of Mary Shelley, the author of Frankenstein, and her creation of one of the most famous monsters in history. Fans celebrate with movie marathons, book readings, and lightning-themed snacks.
holidays.origin: Observed on Mary Shelley's birthday, August 30, 1797. She wrote the novel as a teenager during a ghost story contest on a gloomy summer holiday in Switzerland.
holidays.funFact: Mary Shelley was only 18 when she conceived the story, and Frankenstein is the name of the scientist, not the monster, a mix-up people still make today.

holidays.name: Slinky Day
holidays.description: A bouncy celebration of the spring toy that walks down stairs, makes a satisfying sound, and gets tangled beyond repair. Fans play with Slinkys, race them down staircases, and marvel at their simple physics.
holidays.origin: Observed as a nod to the Slinky, invented by naval engineer Richard James in the 1940s after he saw a tension spring fall off a shelf and keep moving.
holidays.funFact: The first batch of 400 Slinkys sold out in 90 minutes at a Philadelphia department store in 1945, and the toy has an iconic jingle that's one of the longest-running in advertising history.

holidays.name: Beach Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to hitting the sand, soaking up the last rays of summer, and building questionable sandcastles before the season ends. Bring sunscreen, a towel, and the willingness to find sand in your shoes for weeks.
holidays.origin: An informal late-summer observance tied to the end of the summer vacation season, as Labor Day weekend approaches in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Sand is not just one thing: beach sand can be made of coral, volcanic rock, or even parrotfish poop, which is a major source of sand on tropical beaches.
